parameters.name: Rhythm display
parameters.explanation: The display shows the ECG from the selected signal source. Verify the source and signal quality, and interpret the rhythm with the patient assessment and arrest algorithm.

parameters.name: Energy setting
parameters.explanation: The selected energy is the intended shock setting in joules. A trained operator selects it using the resuscitation algorithm, defibrillator instructions and local protocol.

parameters.name: Charge state
parameters.explanation: A charged indication means the defibrillator is ready to deliver the selected shock. Rhythm indication, a clear safety check and an authorized operator are still required before delivery.

safety_concepts.text: Perform and call a safety check so nobody touches the patient or bed at the moment of shock; do not defibrillate during manual chest compressions, even with gloves.
Pads are preferred over paddles when available; if paddles are used apply firm force and good contact to limit arcing.
Keep the pre-shock pause as short as possible: compressions continue while the defibrillator charges; a coordinated team can complete manual defibrillation with under 5 seconds of interruption.

monitoring_concepts.text: Resume chest compressions immediately after shock delivery. A combination of clinical and physiological signs of return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) - such as return of consciousness, purposeful movement, an arterial waveform, or a sharp rise in end-tidal CO2 - is a reason to consider stopping compressions for a rhythm check, and a pulse check if the rhythm appears appropriate. On a defibrillator that displays the ECG with chest-compression motion artefact removed, the underlying rhythm may guide whether a rhythm and pulse check is needed roughly every two minutes; no pause is needed if asystole is displayed.

escalation_concepts.text: Call for help early; follow the oxygen-safety steps in unit policy during defibrillation.
